Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Mumbai man pays Rs 330 for Ola ride, leaves car keys in cab and alleges company sent only generic email replies despite repeated requests for help; driver returns keys for free, consumer commission di
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





MUMBAI: A district consumer commission has dismissed a complaint against cab aggregator Ola, holding that generic customer support emails about a passenger’s forgotten belongings do not constitute deficiency in service. The forum rejected the rider’s claim for damages, awarded no compensation and closed the case without costs.“No material has been placed before us at the admission stage to indicate that the opposite party deliberately withheld assistance, caused the loss of the keys, or adopted any deceptive or unfair practice,” the commission said.The commission said a cab-booking platform is expected to extend reasonable assistance when a passenger reports an article left behind. However, dissatisfaction with email responses, without material showing a failure to provide reasonable assistance, cannot automatically amount to deficiency in service or unfair trade practice.“The complaint essentially arises from the complainant's dissatisfaction with the assistance provided after the cab journey had been completed, despite the eventual return of the keys without cost. Accordingly, the complaint is liable to be dismissed at the admission stage,” the commission said.The complaint was filed in 2026 by Ghatkopar-based Hardik Shah against ANI Technologies Pvt Ltd. Shah alleged that Ola failed to provide effective assistance after he accidentally left his keys in a cab booked through its mobile app.Shah booked an Ola cab and paid Rs 330 at the end of the ride. He later realised, on June 17, 2026, that he had left his car keys in the vehicle and tried to contact the driver through the app.According to Shah, after several attempts, the driver voluntarily returned the keys on June 19 without charging him anything. His grievance was that Ola's email support provided only generic responses and did not offer any meaningful assistance.Since the matter was dismissed at the admission stage, Ola's detailed defence was not recorded. The commission considered Shah's complaint and the documents he submitted before deciding whether the case disclosed grounds to proceed.The bench of president Pradeep G Kadu and member Gauri M Kapse said the cab ride had been completed and there was no allegation of misconduct by the driver during the journey or of overcharging. It noted that Shah had lost possession of the keys because he had inadvertently left them in the cab.
Article Summary: The complaint was filed in 2026 by Ghatkopar-based Hardik Shah against ANI Technologies Pvt Ltd. Shah alleged that Ola failed to provide effective assistance after he accidentally left his keys in a cab booked through its mobile app. The forum rejected the rider's claim for damages, awarded no compensation and closed the case without costs.

Microsoft Outlook outage hits thousands globally, nearly 1.3L users report email issues

Microsoft Outlook suffered a major outage on Thursday, leaving tens of thousands of users unable to access their emails, as the company worked to restore services and limit the disruption.According to outage tracker Downdetector, nearly 130,000 users reported problems with Outlook shortly after 1 pm Eastern Time (1800 GMT). The number of reports subsequently declined, with around 60,000 users still reporting issues as of 3 pm Eastern Time (2000 GMT).Microsoft initially said it was investigating reports of service disruptions in the Americas but later confirmed that the issue could affect Microsoft 365 connectivity across all regions.Microsoft 365 is the company's cloud-based subscription service that includes applications such as Outlook and Teams.In an update on X, Microsoft said it had identified elevated load across parts of its infrastructure in multiple regions as a likely cause of the connectivity problems."We've determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors," the company said."We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," it added.Microsoft said it had paused all deployments, redirected additional traffic away from the affected infrastructure and begun restarting impacted servers to restore services.Thousands of users also reported difficulties accessing Microsoft Teams. Earlier on Thursday, the company said it had “successfully restored” issues affecting Teams in North America, although some users continued to report connectivity problems.

Article Title: As board weighs CEO Jensen Huang's 'exit', Nvidia shares fall 8% after report of second affair
Article Text:
Nvidia stocks had gained in actual stock market trading before the reports on board considering CEO's ouster

Nvidia shares fell 8 per cent in after-hours trading on Wednesday after reports that the company's board was preparing to discuss the future of CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations of two extramarital relationships, including one involving a businesswoman suspected by US intelligence officials of having links to Chinese intelligence services.After-hours trading takes place after the regular market session closes and is not necessarily representative of how a stock will perform when the market reopens.Nvidia's stock has come under significant pressure amid the controversy, with the company losing around $430 billion in market value over Monday and Tuesday as its shares fell a combined 9.5%. However, Nvidia shares had recovered 2.9% during Wednesday's regular trading session before plunging more than 8% after the closing bell.This comes as the Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Nvidia's board was preparing to meet as early as Thursday to discuss Huang's future. CBS News reporter also said in a post on X that the board was preparing to discuss the CEO's position, with the Trump administration aware of plans to remove him. Various reports have also claimed that the board is reportedly looking for a temporary chief to take over from Huang.The developments came after the New York Times reported another alleged relationship between Huang and Nvidia vice president Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to him. The newspaper, citing five people who worked at the company, said the relationship had not been previously reported. The report also raised questions about Nvidia's workplace policies, which ask employees to avoid situations involving potential conflicts of interest, including personal relationships.Read more: Trump administration aware of plans to oust Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang - report Huang, who acknowledged one of the reported relationships in a letter to employees on Sunday, admitted being unfaithful to his wife and apologised for violating their trust. Nvidia's board has reportedly launched an investigation into the matter, led by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.Huang "was the one who led the marvelous rise of Nvidia," said Bruce Zaro, managing director at Granite Wealth Management in Plymouth, Massachusetts., as quoted by Reuters. "I guess the question would be, can someone step up if Jensen has to resign or is forced out?"Meanwhile, on Wall Street, major US stock indexes ended higher on Wednesday, supported by gains in technology shares after upbeat results from CoreWeave lifted optimism around AI-related investments. The S&P 500 rose 1.31% to 7,619.38, the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.60% to 25,466.19, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 0.49% to 52,486.49. The S&P 500 technology sector climbed 2.7%.

Article Title: Norwegian journalist claims MHA cancelled her visa for Hyderabad event
Article Text:
Helle Lyng Svendsen was slated to address the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad on November 14, but faced an unexpected setback

HYDERABAD: Norwegian commentator Helle Lyng Svendsen Wednesday said her Indian visa was cancelled just a day after it was issued and barely 10 minutes before she was to leave for the airport to board a flight to Hyderabad for the Bharat Summit.Svendsen was invited to speak at a panel on 'The Future of Media' at the summit on Nov 14. This was to be her first visit to India.The development comes months after Svendsen aimed a question PM Modi during his visit to Oslo on May 18, asking why he was not taking questions from journalists. This was after Modi and Norwegian PM Jonas Gahr Store had finished making at a joint appearance before the media and were walking away.In a post on X, Svendsen said the cancellation had come on "orders from above" in the home ministry. In a video message, she questioned the Union home minister why her visa was cancelled.During PM Modi’s Oslo visit, Svenden had also reportedly questioned MEA secretary (west) Sibi George over India’s human rights record, asking why Norway should trust a country where such “violations “ happen.In an email interaction with TOI on Wednesday, the commentator with Oslo-based newspaper Dagsavisen said the Indian embassy in Oslo informed her that she would not be allowed to enter India but did not explain why.She said the organisers had informed her last week that political clearance had been granted for her participation. After submitting the required documents on Nov 5, she was informed on Nov 10 that her passport, with the visa, was ready for collection.“The Indian embassy called me 10 minutes before I was leaving for the airport to tell me that my visa would not be valid upon entry to India. They did not want to elaborate to me in writing why it had happened, but apologised for the inconvenience,” she told TOI.Svendsens said that subsequently received an email from the embassy confirming that her visa had been cancelled and was no longer valid for travel. She said she had not been asked to submit any further documents or clarifications before the decision.After her attempt to question PM Modi and her exchange with an MEA secretary, Svendsen was promptly embraced by the opposition and activists back home. She extended support to and lauded CJP’s protests against govt.In the video, Svendsen questioned whether the visa decision was linked to her interaction with Modi in Oslo and her subsequent criticism of the PM and his govt.“It is very unfortunate how much of a hassle it is to host a political conference in the world’s largest democracy,” she said.Svendsen said she had not yet approached Norwegian authorities and would evaluate her next steps.Reacting to the incident, the Indian National Congress , in a post on X, wrote: “Why are Modi and his govt so afraid of questions?”
Article Summary: Svendsen was invited to speak at a panel on 'The Future of Media' at the summit on Nov 14. This was to be her first visit to India. The development comes months after Svendsen aimed a question PM Modi during his visit to Oslo.

HYDERABAD: A 44-year-old stock market investor has been arrested for allegedly bludgeoning to death a defence PSU executive’s wife at their flat in Dhatu Nagar in Meerpet on Wednesday evening. After a preliminary investigation, police arrested the stock trader, who lives in the same apartment complex, on Thursday and recovered the jewellery he had stolen from the victim’s flat. He reportedly resorted to the crime to tide over his financial woes.The deceased was identified as Anitha Arun Kumar, 34, wife of Mishra Dhatu Nigam Ltd (MIDHANI) deputy general manager Arun Kumar Venugopal.According to the Meerpet police, Arun used to drop his two children at school every morning, while Anitha used to bring them home in the evening.Around 8:20am on Wednesday, Arun dropped his two children, an 11-year-old and an eight-year-old, at school. As Anitha did not turn up at the school in the evening, they reached home on their own.“The children found Anitha lying in a pool of blood on the bedroom floor. They called Arun from her phone. He rushed to the flat and shifted Anitha to a private hospital in an ambulance where she was declared dead,” Meerpet inspector B Shobhan said.Police also reached the crime scene.During the preliminary probe, police found that an unidentified assailant had entered the flat and gagged Anitha. “She was hit on the head with an iron box. She died due to the bleeding head injury,” the inspector said. After hitting her with the box, the assailant also tried to strangle her with its cable, police added.The assailant also stole 21 tola gold jewellery, including gold bangles, a gold ring and a chain, from the flat. Police verified CCTV footage at the apartment and surrounding areas. They also questioned neighbours and zeroed in on Raj Kumar, 44, a stock market investor, who lives in a flat above the victim’s in the same apartment.“Raj Kumar had incurred debt of Rs 4 crore due to losses in stock market investments. Due to his financial condition, he decided to kill and steal from the victim, whom he knew would be alone in the flat. The accused’s family members were not at home when the incident happened.We recovered the stolen gold from his possession. The crime was committed by Raj Kumar alone,” the inspector said. The body of Anitha was handed over to her family on Thursday after the post-mortem examination.On Arun’s complaint, police registered a case under Section 103 (1) (Murder), 305 (a) (Theft in a dwelling house) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita on Wednesday night. According to police, accused Raj Kumar was involved in some cheque bounce cases.
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Anitha Arun Kumar, 34, wife of Mishra Dhatu Nigam Ltd (MIDHANI) deputy general manager. Raj Kumar, 44, a stock market investor, who lives in a flat above the victim’s in the same apartment complex, was arrested on Thursday.

Article Title: Bulldozer is now UP’s brand, says CM Yogi Adityanath; invites firms to manufacture

CM Yogi during CNH Industrial’s groundbreaking ceremony

LUCKNOW: Chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday described bulldozers as a brand associated with the state and suggested that CNH Industrial, which is setting up a tractor manufacturing plant in Gautam Budh Nagar, could also manufacture them in Uttar Pradesh “You must have heard about Uttar Pradesh’s bulldozer. Article Title: In 2022, a Kerala woman cleared IELTS and mortgaged her property for a promised UK job; consultancy retained Rs 18.89 lakh from a Rs 20 lakh loan despite failing to arrange visa; consumer panel orders

KOCHI: A woman in Kerala who mortgaged her property to finance a promised job in the UK was left without employment and facing loan liabilities after an overseas recruitment consultancy allegedly failed to deliver on its assurance. The Pathanamthitta District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed the consultancy firm and its associates to pay her Rs 19.49 lakh, including Rs 18.89 lakh retained from a loan raised against her property, Rs 50,000 in compensation and Rs 10,000 towards litigation costs.The woman, a divorcee raising two children, had approached the consultancy in 2022 after completing a healthcare assistant course and clearing the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) examination. She was looking for an opportunity to work in the UK. The consultancy agreed to arrange a job visa for Rs 13.50 lakh. When she told its representatives that she could not afford the amount, they allegedly suggested raising the money through a chitty loan from the Kerala State Financial Enterprises (KSFE).Under the arrangement, she was asked to mortgage her property against a chitty scheme registered in the name of one of the consultancy's associates.She was assured that the loan instalments would be paid only after she found employment abroad.Trusting the promise, she handed over her property documents. The consultancy subsequently arranged a loan of Rs 20 lakh against her property, although the agreed cost of securing the UK job visa was Rs 13.50 lakh. The woman had initially paid the firm Rs 2.50 lakh on May 31, 2023, and received an offer letter. The amount was later returned after the loan was secured. The consultancy also paid Rs 10,266 towards an outstanding loan she had with another bank and gave her Rs 1 lakh for her children's education.However, she questioned why a loan of Rs 20 lakh had been raised when the agreed amount was considerably lower. She alleged that the consultancy failed to arrange the promised visa and stopped responding to her calls. When she visited its office, she learnt that several other people had also allegedly faced similar problems.She subsequently approached the consumer commission, alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practices. In its October 15 order, the commission noted that none of the consultancy's representatives appeared before it.The panel noted that the woman had approached the consultancy after seeing an advertisement on Facebook in 2022. The firm provided assistance to people seeking employment overseas and operated through several associates and employees.The commission also recorded that the woman had lodged a police complaint against the consultancy's representatives. They subsequently agreed to release her property documents after clearing the outstanding liabilities.However, the consultancy defaulted on the chitty loan repayments. KSFE issued a registered notice to both the firm and the woman, asking them to clear the dues under the scheme registered in the firm's name. The panel found that the woman had received only Rs 1.10 lakh from the loan arrangement, including the amount provided for her children's education. The remaining Rs 18.89 lakh was retained by the consultancy and its associates. The commission directed the firm and the other opposite parties to refund Rs 18.89 lakh to the woman within 30 days. It also ordered them to pay Rs 50,000 as compensation and Rs 10,000 towards the cost of proceedings.
Article Summary: The woman, a divorcee raising two children, had approached the consultancy in 2022. She was looking for an opportunity to work in the UK. The consultancy agreed to arrange a job visa for Rs 13.50 lakh. When she told its representatives that she could not afford the amount, they allegedly suggested raising the money through a chitty loan.

HYDERABAD: An irrigation department engineer was arrested after Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) raids across Telangana unearthed assets allegedly worth more than ₹25 crore, including a luxury villa, farmland, multiple plots, gold and investments, in a disproportionate assets case.The ACB’s central investigation unit registered a disproportionate assets case against R Satyanarayana (44), deputy executive engineer in the irrigation and command area development department, Nagarkurnool district, under the Prevention of Corruption Act and carried out simultaneous searches at 10 locations on Thursday.The raids covered Satyanarayana’s residence in Karmanghat, his office in Nagarkurnool, and properties linked to his relatives, family members and alleged benamis in Hyderabad, Wanaparthy and Nagarkurnool.Satyanarayana was at his native village, Shapur in Ghanpur mandal of Wanaparthy district, when the searches began. Article Title: Rupee extends winning streak, breaks below 94 against dollar: What's next
Article Text:
Rupee moves below 94 against US dollar

Crude oil prices cool as hopes of peace grow

Foreign fund inflows add to rupee's support

NEW DELHI: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East.The currency rose 24 paise to 93.74 against the US dollar in early trade. It opened at around 93.85 in the interbank forex market before gaining further. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98 against the greenback.Forex traders said rupee could maintain its positive momentum if diplomatic efforts in the Middle East make progress. Any easing of tensions could reduce the risk premium in crude oil prices, providing further support to the currency.These hopes gained ground over the weekend after US President Donald Trump indicated that further military strikes against Iran were highly unlikely if negotiations progressed and both sides reached a strong agreement.The easing in crude oil prices has been one of the key factors supporting rupee. Brent crude, which had earlier climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. Amit Pabari, managing director of CR Forex Advisors, said improving diplomatic expectations were already having an impact on energy prices."The improvement in diplomatic expectations is already reflecting in energy prices. Brent crude, which had climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. For currency markets, even the possibility of a lasting agreement is important," Pabari said.Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.15% lower at $98.17 per barrel in futures trade. The dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was also down 0.12% at 102.18.Foreign investment activity provided another source of support for the domestic currency. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) purchased equities worth Rs 13,749.82 crore on Friday, according to exchange data.The combination of lower crude prices and stronger foreign fund inflows has supported the rupee's recent gains against the dollar.With rupee now below the 94-per-dollar level, Pabari sees further room for appreciation. He expects the currency to move towards 93.50 and 93.00, while identifying 94.40–94.50 as the immediate resistance zone."With USD/INR breaking below the 94.00 mark, the probability of further rupee appreciation towards 93.50 and 93.00 has increased. On the upside, 94.40–94.50 is likely to act as the immediate resistance zone," Pabari said.Meanwhile, domestic equity markets opened lower on Monday. BSE Sensex fell 93.95 points to 80,919.19, while NSE Nifty declined 30 points to 24,968.80.Separately, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reported that India's foreign exchange reserves declined by $2.691 billion to $717.056 billion in the week ended October 30.
Article Summary: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98.

Article Title: Colette Kress sends her first email to employees as Nvidia interim CEO after Jensen Huang’s resignation: More than anything, I believe in...
Article Text:
Colette Kress, Nvidia’s CFO and now interim CEO, wrote to employees a day after Jensen Huang’s resignation.

Colette Kress will run Nvidia while keeping her CFO job

Nvidia earnings and an all-hands meeting land in Kress' first week

Here is Colette Kress' full email to Nvidia employees

Subject: RE: Statement from NVIDIA Board Chair

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Dear NVIDIAns,

I believe deeply in this company and in its future. More than anything, I believe in each of you, in our customers and partners and in the vital role we play every day in the global economy.

The Board, Estaff and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication.

Thank you.

This company has achieved so much because of the work that all of you bring to it every single day. You are our greatest strength. You will hear more from leadership in the coming days about our future together, and we will host a company meeting on November 18 at 9am PT.

We play a vital role in building the technology that is powering the AI revolution, and we have important work ahead of us. So let's move forward together, with the same determination and commitment that have always defined this company.

Thank you for all you do,

Colette

Colette Kress has sent her first email to Nvidia employees as interim CEO, a day after Jensen Huang quit the company he co-founded 33 years ago. In the email, Kress tells staff that "more than anything" she believes in them. She thanks them for their "resilience, professionalism and continued dedication", and confirms a company-wide meeting on November 18 at 9am PT (10:30pm IST).The email comes at the end of a turbulent week. Nvidia's board put out statements on November 8 and November 10. Then on Thursday, Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately. He left after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Kress sent the email as a reply to the new board chair's statement, and it does not mention Huang by name.Kress has been Nvidia's chief financial officer since September 2013. She will hold both roles until the board names a permanent CEO. Before Nvidia, she spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at Cisco and Microsoft. Investors know her voice well, as she has sat alongside Huang on the company's earnings calls for years.The board has also appointed Harvey C. Jones as Nvidia's first-ever chair. Jones is the former CEO and executive chairman of chip design software firm Synopsys. He said the board has "full confidence" in Kress and expects operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap to continue "without interruption". The search for a permanent CEO will consider internal and external candidates.Kress will not get a quiet start. Nvidia reports its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Tuesday, November 17, with the earnings call at 2pm PT. The employee meeting follows the next morning, US time.Markets have reacted. Nvidia shares opened down more than 13% after the resignation, wiping more than half a trillion dollars off its market value. Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon halved the firm's price target, writing in a note, "We've had enough and prefer to watch from the sidelines."Analysts have named three possible permanent successors: co-founder Chris Malachowsky; Ian Buck, who runs Nvidia's high-performance computing business; and Arm CEO Rene Haas. Who gets the job is the board's call. Until then, Kress is asking employees to stay focused on the work and "move forward together".
Article Summary: Colette Kress has been Nvidia's CFO since September 2013. She will hold both roles until the board names a permanent CEO. In the email, Kress tells staff that "more than anything" she believes in them. She thanks them for their "resilience, professionalism and continued dedication"
